title: Neural Granular Synthesis — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Neural Granular Synthesis's rich face: two walks the Shop made, the crowd-size ladder ending on whether a big crowd is always steady and the lock's attack ending on what sets how hard the lock hits, laid beside the steward's renders, recordings and playable crowds from June to October, with the fingerprint of the words each was made against. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: Two parts of the paragraph, measured on the crowd-size ladder (cycle 7's model; the steward's render_crowd_size.py re-run by the challenger, the face's port by the maker, three crowds per rung each). (1) 'a single grain is a snippet of sound with no discernible pitch': true only for a grain a few cycles long. The ladder's 90 ms grain holds 29.7 cycles of its 330 Hz pitch and is a note; at 3 ms it is one cycle, a click. What the crowd adds is steadiness, not pitch. (2) 'Stack thousands of grains … and suddenly you have color': on the steward's original, an uncoupled crowd's gappiness (10 ms loudness frames, std ÷ mean) comes within about a fifth of steady noise from about 32 neurons (1.21×, about 190 grains a second), about an eighth from 64 (1.12×), and within a tenth only at 256 (1.09×); the port reads a little lower (1.24× at 16, 1.08× at 64), inside the original's spread between crowds. Locked (K 1.6), it stays 5.2–6.1× the floor at every size from 4 to 512. So stability lives in the population only while its members keep their own time. Proposed: 'In granular synthesis, a single grain is a snippet: a short one has no discernible pitch, and even a long one is a single event. Stack a few dozen independent grains a second, and more, with careful control over their distribution, density and envelope, and the events fuse into color, texture and intentional timbre. The magic is in the population, not the grain, as long as the population keeps its own time: a crowd that fires together is one big grain, at any size.'

The Lumpiness line: 'An evenly spread crowd locks like a switch; a lumpy one starts agreeing early and arrives softly. This, not the pacemaker share, sets how hard the lock hits.' Measured on crowd_engine.js (512 neurons; the steward's lumpiness.json reproduced to the third decimal), each crowd read on its own in 1.25% steps of tightness; the challenger ran ten lumpy crowds per life on the steward's own engine. Holds: an even crowd snaps at any pacemaker share (agreement jumps 0.46 in one step with none, 0.34 with half; half pacemakers lift agreement below the lock 0.07 → 0.19 without softening the jump). Holds: lumpy crowds agree early (0.12–0.27 below the lock). Not reliably: with no pacemakers lumpy crowds jump 0.13–0.46 (two of ten at 0.46, as hard as an even crowd), each locking at its own place (0.92–1.04× the edge); every single crowd's width (0.016–0.090) is below the averaged 0.111, also on the steward's own grid, so 0.111 partly measures scatter between crowds. With half pacemakers lumpy crowds do arrive softly (jumps 0.07–0.17). Wrong: 'not the pacemaker share' — even the steward's averaged widths go 0.111 → 0.173 with half pacemakers, and cycle 15 said 'pacemakers do soften the lock, but only in a lumpy crowd'. Proposed: 'An evenly spread crowd locks like a switch, whatever its pacemakers; a lumpy one starts agreeing early, and with pacemakers in it arrives softly. Lumpiness opens the way to a soft lock; the pacemaker share then sets how soft.'

The threshold variance line: 'low variance = synchronized firing'. This rests wholly on the steward's cycle 8 data (timbre-map.json, 136 crowds), not re-run by the maker or the challenger. In it every spread from 0.02 to 0.40 drifts at K = 0 (r 0.07–0.09), and each first passes r 0.5 just past K = 4σ/π: spread moves the lock, it doesn't synchronize. Caveats: σ is a rate spread standing in for threshold variance, which cycle 8 calls argued, not tested; and the narrowest uncoupled crowd already has pitch clarity 0.85 at r 0.07, so low variance buys a clear pitch without synchrony. Proposed: 'High variance = heterogeneous neurons that need more coupling to lock; low variance = a crowd that locks at weaker coupling (the lock sits at K = 4σ/π), and sounds clearer even before it locks'.

offers.section: Statistical Mechanics: The Mathematics of Emergence
offers.what: The synchrony index line names r, the Kuramoto order parameter, as the measure of phase coherence and reads 0 as incoherent. That global r is the mean over the whole crowd, and a traveling wave falsifies the reading: re-run on kernel_lib's traveling-wave regime (128 neurons, narrow kernel, a seeded q = 3 twist, 30 s settle, three seeds), global r is 0.002–0.018 while neighbors are locked. How locked depends on the window local coherence is read over: 0.98–0.99 at 0.01 of the ring, 0.91–0.95 at 0.02, 0.71–0.79 at 0.04, and only 0.25–0.39 at kernel_lib's default 0.08. A window must be narrower than one arm of the wave (a third of the ring here). The page's own raster section names diagonal bands, so it already holds both halves. Proposed, added to the line: 'a global r near 0 can also mean a traveling wave, where neighbors are locked but the crowd as a whole cancels; coherence read over a window narrower than the wave tells them apart'.

'What is the minimum population size for perceptually stable timbres?' has a measured answer the page doesn't carry (cycle 7, 2026-09-24; re-run by the challenger on the steward's original and by the maker on the port): it depends on r, and the dependence is graded. At about six firings a second per neuron and 90 ms grains: uncoupled, the crowd comes within about a fifth of steady noise from about 32 neurons and about an eighth from 64 (about 190–380 grains a second, on the original); near the lock (K 0.2) it reaches 1.14–1.17× only at 512; locked, no size does, staying 5–6× grainier than the floor from 4 to 512. Brightness settles sooner, by about 16 (the steward's number, not re-run). Untested: other firing rates and grain lengths, and the ear. Proposed, under the question: '— measured (2026-09-24, re-run 2026-11-03): it depends on r. Uncoupled, a few dozen neurons (about 200–400 grains a second at 90 ms) reach a steady texture; near the lock it takes hundreds; locked, no number does, because a crowd that fires together is one grain. Coupling is a density control as well as a pitch control.'

Two more questions have the steward's measured answers. This rests wholly on cycle 8's timbre-map.json, not re-run by the maker or the challenger. 'Can we tune threshold variance to target specific regions of timbre space?': not on its own; it moves the lock, and every spread lies on one curve against coupling ÷ spread (built into this model, a confirmation, not a discovery), so an instrument needs one knob, coupling per unit of disorder. σ is a rate spread standing in for threshold variance. 'Does coupling strength correlate with a dimension of timbre space?': yes, brightness, on the locked side: at the lock the tone goes dark at every spread (about 760 → 326–395 Hz), then brightens as coupling ÷ spread rises, toward about 700 Hz only for narrow spreads within the swept range (748 Hz at σ 0.02, 519 at 0.2, 354 at 0.4). Proposed: a short measured note under each, as the pacemaker question already has.

An offer for the Action Potential Oscillator face, not this page: its Population Dynamics offer and crowd piece call coupling 'like a lowpass' from one coupling setting (3× each shape's half-lock). This face's timbre map shows brightness climbing back past the lock as coupling rises (σ 0.2: 765 Hz unlocked, 326 at the lock, 519 at K 0.8, still below unlocked). So 'lowpass' holds against the scattered crowd, and more coupling opens it again. Different engines (neuropulse.dsp there, phase neurons here); no contradiction, one line of tension: 'locking darkens the crowd; tightening past the lock brightens it again, though not back to the scattered color'.

verdicts.why: Gathered record that makes the opening's noisy-whispers-to-stable-timbre arc audible on the population's knobs; caption matches cycle 12 (snap near 8.5 s, 128 neurons, the phrase).
The meters under the take, needed to follow what the knobs did; caption accurate.

pieces.title: the crowd in one take · 13 October
pieces.caption: 51 seconds of the playable crowd, 128 neurons: hiss, then the snap into a tone near 8.5 s, a dead-still tone, pacemakers fading in until it breathes, a wide vibrato, the core coming apart under the edge, and a short phrase, A C D E D A, on the living tone. Noisy whispers to a stable timbre and back, played on the population's knobs.

pieces.title: the meters under the take
pieces.caption: Tightness, life, agreement and pitch wobble under the one-take above, so you can follow what the knobs did while you listen.

pieces.file: Neural Granular Synthesis — rich — crowd-size ladder.html
pieces.title: how many grains make a color? · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **Is a big enough crowd always steady?** One neuron firing 90 ms grains, then four, then the crowd grown rung by rung to 512, with a meter reading how grainy the sound is against steady noise of the same color. The last step locks the crowd and climbs again. The engine is the steward's cycle 7 ladder, ported; the headless re-run beside it matches the steward's numbers within the scatter between crowds.

pieces.title: brightness and gappiness by crowd size · 24 September
pieces.caption: The steward's measurement behind the walk. Left, brightness wobble: it reaches the noise floor by about 16 neurons, so brightness is not what sets the minimum. Right, gappiness: the uncoupled crowd falls to the floor, the locked one never leaves 1.4. Bottom, rasters at 8, 32, 128 and 512, uncoupled above and locked below.

verdicts.why: The persistent population the section describes, playable; shows rather than tests, but the section's claim is what to build and this is it. Caption accurate, no lumpiness knob confirmed.

pieces.title: the crowd, playable · 13 October
pieces.caption: **The persistent population you can play.** A pad sets tightness across and life (the pacemaker share) up, with the theory's edge, 1/(1 − life), drawn on it; keys A to K play notes. Below it, a live raster and phase wheel. The neurons are never created or destroyed: the same crowd carries its phases across every audio buffer. It has no lumpiness knob yet; the walk under Population-Level Parameters runs the same engine with one.

verdicts.why: A test that comes out partly against the text; walks up one knob at a time; engine byte for byte crowd_engine.js; the in-page measurement matched the headless one exactly. Note: step 3 asserts lumpy crowds 'arrive at the tone gradually' before the test qualifies it; 'can arrive' would be truer.
Byte-identical to the owner's ignored original and tracked; timings check (edge at 4 s, passes at 0, 9.6, 19.2 s); seed 3 at half pacemakers does arrive softly (jump 0.149).
The steward's averaged curves; the caption's 'part of the averaged softness is crowds locking at different places' is confirmed (every single crowd's width below the averaged 0.111).

pieces.file: Neural Granular Synthesis — rich — lock attack.html
pieces.title: how hard does the lock hit? · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **Does lumpiness, and not the pacemaker share, set how hard the lock hits?** Tightness alone throws a switch; pacemakers move it to 1/(1 − life); lumpiness lets it soften. The last step measures four crowds on this page, each lumpy one three times, and reads both the steward's width and the biggest single jump. The engine is crowd_engine.js, byte for byte; the headless check reproduces the steward's sweep to the third decimal.

pieces.title: three ramps through the lock · 18 October
pieces.caption: Half pacemakers, 512 neurons, tightness ramping from 0.8 to 1.15 of the edge over 7 s and held 2 s, three times: even (0 to 9 s), half lumpy (9.6 s), fully lumpy (19.2 s). The ramp crosses the edge at 4 s into each pass. Listen for the even crowd's snap and the lumpy ones swimming in.

sections.heading: Statistical Mechanics: The Mathematics of Emergence

verdicts.why: Tests that the aggregate is the control surface across 136 crowds. Note: the caption could carry cycle 8's own caveat that the coupling ÷ spread collapse is built into the model, a confirmation, not a discovery.
Times match cycle 8 (snap about 4.7 s, dissolve about 19 s, release about 32 s).

pieces.title: the timbre map · 24 September
pieces.caption: 136 crowds of 128 neurons at audio rate. Agreement, harmonicity, pitch clarity and brightness over coupling and spread, with the theory's lock K = 4σ/π dashed: below it a buzzy smear, past it a clean tone that goes dark at the lock and brightens as coupling rises. Panel F: every spread collapses onto one curve against coupling ÷ spread, so the aggregate is the control surface, and a single number. The steward's own caveat from cycle 8: the collapse is built into this model, so it is a confirmation, not a discovery; and σ is a rate spread standing in for threshold variance, argued rather than tested.

pieces.title: three walks across the map · 24 September
pieces.caption: 36 s at matched loudness. Coupling rises (the smear snaps into a dark tone at about 4.7 s, then brightens); held while the spread widens (the tone dissolves near 19 s); coupling falls (it releases near 32 s).

sections.heading: The Raster Plot as Pedagogical Tool

verdicts.why: A test you run: makes the three named patterns and the unnamed chimera; the wave's global r 0.00 with neighbourhoods locked re-ran (local r 0.91–0.95 at a 0.02 window). No AudioContext, so 'it doesn't sound' is true.
Accurate to cycle 6; the chimera is the regime the section doesn't name.
Accurate to cycle 6; ring as stereo field.

pieces.title: raster explorer · 24 September
pieces.caption: **Make stripes, scatter and diagonal bands yourself.** One row per neuron on a ring, presets for drift, lock, traveling wave and chimera, and a strip down the right edge showing each neuron's local agreement. The wave is why the strip is there: its global r reads 0.00 while every neighborhood is locked. It draws; it doesn't sound. The recording beside it is the sound.

pieces.title: four regimes on one ring
pieces.caption: Drift, lock, traveling wave and chimera, 128 neurons each after a 30 s settle, each with its local-agreement profile. The chimera, half locked and half drifting from one population, is the regime the section's three readings don't name.

pieces.title: the four regimes, heard · stereo
pieces.caption: 31 s, about 7 s each: drift, lock, wave, chimera. The ring is the stereo field, so the wave's spikes sweep across the speakers and the chimera puts its locked half on the left. Headphones help.

verdicts.why: Answers part of the liveliness question by ear. Note: the caption's '10 cents at 5%' names a share the recording doesn't play; use '13 cents at 10%, 21 at 20%' from cycle 9's table.
Byte-identical to the owner's original; caption matches cycle 16.

pieces.title: six pacemaker shares on a locked tone · 24 September
pieces.caption: 25 s at coupling 0.4: pacemaker share 0 (dead still), 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.5 and 0.65 (on the edge), 3.6 s each, levelled. Measured: 13 cents of pitch wobble at 10%, 21 at 20%, the pitch still clear to half.

pieces.title: the surge before the lock · 18 October
pieces.caption: 13 s: an even crowd of 512 held at 0.9 of its edge, 6 s with no pacemakers, then 6 s with half. In the second half it lunges toward agreement and falls back a few times a second.

pieces.title: how much the agreement swings
pieces.caption: Left, agreement over time just under the lock at 0, 20 and 50% pacemakers; right, the swing grows with the share (0.05, 0.08, 0.16).

pieces.title: the crowd-size ladder · 24 September
pieces.caption: 56 s: eight rungs uncoupled, 4 to 512 neurons, then the same eight locked, 3 s each at matched loudness. The uncoupled crowd's grains fuse by the middle rungs; the locked crowd pulses six times a second at every size. The walk under The Core Insight lets you climb it yourself.
